system_prompt:
You are distilling one chapter of a guitar method book into a short summary.

The user will give you a chapter file with topic-organized verbatim quotes
plus the human-rationale notes for each. Write a one-paragraph summary (4-7
sentences) that captures:

  - what this chapter teaches (the techniques, concepts, rules, examples)
  - the master's characteristic moves visible in this chapter (if any)
  - the load-bearing terminology this chapter introduces

Reference the topic labels from the chapter file when useful. Do not invent
information not present in the chapter. If the chapter is biographical or
introductory rather than instructional, say so explicitly.

Output just the paragraph — no preamble, no JSON, no markdown formatting.

<<<CHAPTER FILE
# Chapter 16 — HOUSTON, WE HAVE A PROBLEM

_Pages 21-22._

> **Verbatim-quote constraint.** The quotes below are exact substrings of the raw transcript produced by `pdftotext`. The transcript may contain extraction artifacts where the book's typeface confuses the tool — e.g. `7irst` or `<irst` for `first`, `speci7ic` for `specific`. **Do NOT manually fix these in this file**: the quote-fidelity validator compares against the raw transcript, so a 'fixed' quote will fail verification and break Stage 2 idempotency. If a future pipeline iteration adds artifact-normalization, it must normalize the transcript and these files together.

## 4-way close on guitar

> Since 4-way close is often very difficult on the guitar, all of
> the above would be an excellent FIRST PASS. [As was mentioned in the text from Volume I, all
> of us guitarists still should try to find as many playable voicings for 4-way close as we
> can...especially using open strings.]

**Significance (p. 21).** Practical rule for guitarists on attempting 4-way close.

## Cycles 2 and 7 exception

> Cycles 2 and 7 have two different voice-leadings. [One for 4-way close, and
> another one for the other five voicing types...] {Neither of these voice-leadings is particularly
> pleasing from a sound perspective...}

**Significance (p. 21).** Structural exception in the system.

## Diatonic 5th voice-crossing

> It involves the
> interval of a diatonic 5th that occurs in the movement from one inversion to the next within
> the same chord. For guitarists, this could lead to potential problems with voices crossing each
> other if we had chosen to uses voice-leadings that were more pleasing from a sound perspec-
> tive.

**Significance (p. 21).** Root cause of voice-leading compromise.

## Spread cluster caution

> All of these spread cluster voicings are extremely interesting. [And mostly unknown,
> until now...] And many of them are difficult to play on the guitar, so BE VERY CAREFUL!!!

**Significance (p. 22).** Explicit difficulty warning.

## M-Lode voice-leading basis

> All of the M-Lode is based on voice-leading.

**Significance (p. 22).** Foundational principle of the entire method.

## Scope of voicings found

> For the first time in the history of music on our planet, all of the 3-part and 4-part
> voicings that exist within the Major Scale, the Melodic Minor Scale and the Harmonic Minor
> Scale have been found.

**Significance (p. 22).** Defines scope and claim of method — three scales, all voicings.

>
> Number of different voicings for these chords found: 800+
